extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational linguistics researchers, evaluators of creative writing, and practitioners studying automated literary evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Applying an adapted Consensual Assessment Technique (CAT) to have large language models perform comparative evaluations of poetry, then measuring agreement with a proxy ground truth. The study tests protocol choices (e.g., forced-choice ranking, small randomized batches) and compares LLMs to non-expert human judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensual Assessment Technique (CAT) adapted for LLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapts the Consensual Assessment Technique (CAT) for Large Language Models (LLMs), introducing a novel methodology for poetry evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CAT principles with LLMs to produce judgments intended to reflect consensus quality assessments of poems. The paper demonstrates this approach on a 90-poem dataset and frames CAT as the core evaluation methodology for LLM-based poetic assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forced-choice ranking within small, randomized batches
rubrics_metrics.description: The method leverages forced-choice ranking within small, randomized batches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer forced-choice (relative) ranking over absolute numeric ratings and present poems in small randomized groups to raters (LLMs or humans). In the study this protocol enabled Claude-3-Opus to achieve very high agreement with the ground truth (reported SRC=0.87).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground truth proxy: publication venue
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground truth used in the study is based on publication venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use publication venue as a proxy label of poem quality for evaluation experiments. The paper's reported results (e.g., correlations) are computed against this venue-based ground truth built from the 90-poem dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spearman's Rank Correlation (SRC) with ground truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Spearman's Rank Correlation (SRC) is used to quantify agreement between model/human rankings and the ground truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure rank-order agreement using SRC. Example results reported: Claude-3-Opus SRC = 0.87 with the ground truth, versus best human non-expert evaluation SRC = 0.38, illustrating the metric's use for comparative performance claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter-rater reliability of assessments is reported as an indicator of robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess consistency among multiple raters (LLMs or humans); high inter-rater reliability supports the stability and robustness of the chosen evaluation protocol. The paper notes high inter-rater reliability for LLM assessments under their protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative evaluation framework
rubrics_metrics.description: A comparative framework for assessing poetry (relative judgments across items) is advocated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame poetry evaluation as comparative judgments between items rather than isolated absolute scores to leverage LLM strengths in relative evaluation. The paper presents this comparative framework as generalizable to other creative domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline comparison to non-expert human judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare LLM assessment performance against non-expert human judges as a baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include non-expert human baselines when evaluating LLMs; the study reports LLMs dramatically outperforming non-expert human evaluation under their protocol (example SRC values provided).
